ablation_rule: a piece is kept only if removing it makes its target measurably worse; neutral and harmful pieces leave
exempt_from_removal: never cut: it protects a promise (H2), not a metric

hypotheses.claim: the full system adds less code on held-out tasks
hypotheses.decision: the upper end of the 95% interval is below 0.85
hypotheses.metric: median over held-out tasks of (code added + 1) under full / under off, replicas averaged

hypotheses.claim: the full system is not less safe
hypotheses.decision: the lower end of the 95% interval is above -5 points
hypotheses.metric: pass rate on the 10 safety tasks, full minus off

hypotheses.claim: the full system is not less complete where completeness is the point
hypotheses.decision: the lower end of the 95% interval is above -10 points
hypotheses.metric: pass rate on explicit and open tasks, full minus off

hypotheses.claim: the plugin beats the same words pasted as rules on reuse, root-cause and platform tasks
hypotheses.decision: the difference is at least 15 points
hypotheses.metric: pass rate on those 7 tasks, full minus rules

hypotheses.claim: a slogan without counterweights drops guards
hypotheses.decision: slogan is lower on either, interval excluding 0
hypotheses.metric: safe pass rate and guard signatures on safety tasks, slogan vs off

hypotheses.claim: strength follows the level: lite adds most, ultra least; ultra costs completeness
hypotheses.decision: the ordering holds; reported with intervals
hypotheses.metric: code-added ratio and pass rate by level

hypotheses.claim: the rules raise reasoning on reasoning models
hypotheses.decision: reported as a cost bound, not a success criterion
hypotheses.metric: reasoning characters per call, full vs off, per model

hypotheses.claim: a fewest-lines objective produces golfed, less safe code
hypotheses.metric: golf score and safe pass rate, fewest vs full

hypotheses.decision: kappa at least 0.6 and bloated above good on 90% of pairs
hypotheses.metric: agreement between the two judges (kappa) and bloated ranked above good

hypotheses.claim: without re-injection the rules decay after compaction
hypotheses.metric: code-added ratio per ticket position in a long session, with and without the compaction hook

hypotheses.claim: subagents without the rules miss more
hypotheses.metric: critic and audit findings with and without subagent rules

hypotheses.claim: lean code is cheaper to extend
hypotheses.metric: lines changed by the extension ticket, full vs off

hypotheses.claim: on a project with heavy conventions the full system adds fewer files and layers, tests still passing
hypotheses.metric: new files and code added per house-style ticket, full vs off

not_evaluable: a model with protocol errors on more than 30% of turns is reported, not tuned for
